findings.problem: ShardWorkflow uses a flat struct with independent booleans instead of a typed state machine with enforced transitions
findings.failure_mode: Callers can construct ShardWorkflow with is_validated=false, is_sent=true, status="pending" — an impossible state the domain model should never permit
findings.fix: Replace the struct fields with a ShardState enum (e.g. Pending, Validated, Sent) that encodes valid transitions; constructors return Result<ShardWorkflow, StateError>

findings.problem: pub status: String stores lifecycle status as a free-form string instead of a closed enum
findings.failure_mode: Any arbitrary string is accepted ("sent", "SENT", "sent ", "deleted", ""); callers cannot exhaustively match; the domain loses all state-machine guarantees
findings.fix: Replace `status: String` with `status: ShardStatus` enum; derive From for known conversions; match exhaustively at call sites

findings.problem: pub is_validated: bool and pub is_sent: bool encode lifecycle flags as independent booleans
findings.failure_mode: Two independent booleans create 16 reachable states; only 4 are valid (not-validated/not-sent, not-validated/sent, validated/not-sent, validated/sent), but the domain likely intends a linear progression (pending → validated → sent) — the remaining 12 states are silently reachable
findings.fix: Replace both booleans with a single ShardState enum whose variants carry only the data needed for that stage (e.g. Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 }); callers must pattern-match variants exhaustively

findings.problem: pub is_sent: bool and pub sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64> are independent fields — Option can be Some while is_sent is false, or is_sent true while Option is None
findings.failure_mode: is_sent=true with sent_at_epoch_ms=None loses the sent timestamp; is_sent=false with sent_at_epoch_ms=Some(…) claims a sent time without the flag; both are domain-invalid but constructible with no validation
findings.fix: Embed sent_at_epoch_ms inside the Sent variant of the ShardState enum so the timestamp and the sent flag are co-located and co-enforced

findings.problem: pub id: String is a raw primitive exposed as a public field with no domain invariants
findings.failure_mode: Any string including empty, whitespace-only, or malformed IDs is accepted; callers cannot distinguish a valid shard ID from a random string at the type level
findings.fix: Define `pub struct ShardId(String)` or better `pub struct ShardId(Uuid)` with a smart constructor `ShardId::parse(s) -> Result<Self, IdError>`; make the field private behind a getter

findings.problem: mark_sent mutates ShardWorkflow fields directly and is exposed as a pure-looking function that performs hidden mutation on the domain type
findings.failure_mode: The function signature suggests a pure transformation (takes ShardWorkflow, returns ShardWorkflow) but sets mutable fields internally, violating the functional core principle that domain types are immutable by construction; callers may pass already-sent items and double-set state
findings.fix: Replace with `fn transition_to_sent(item: ShardWorkflow) -> Result<ShardWorkflow, TransitionError>` that inspects the current state enum variant and returns an error if the item is already sent

findings.problem: ShardWorkflow fields are pub and constructible with raw primitives — no smart constructor or fallible parse exists, so raw primitives cross the parse boundary directly into domain code
findings.failure_mode: External callers can construct ShardWorkflow { id: "", status: "", is_validated: false, is_sent: false, sent_at_epoch_ms: None } via a struct literal with zero validation, violating parse-don't-validate
findings.fix: Add `impl ShardWorkflow` with a `parse` or `try_new` method that accepts primitives, validates each field with fallible smart constructors, and returns Result<ShardWorkflow, ParseError>; make all struct fields private
